prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: spaCy Pipeline and Attributes
area.rationale: spaCy basics: processing text, Doc/Token/Span containers, lexical attributes, pre-trained models, POS tagging, dependencies, NER, lemmatization, and rule-based matching.

candidates.label: Processing text and exploring documents, tokens, and spans in spaCy
candidates.description: Use spacy.blank to create a pipeline and process text into a Doc. Understand tokenization as the process of splitting text into tokens. Access tokens by index and create spans.
coverage_criteria: Write code to create a blank Portuguese pipeline, process 'Olá mundo', and confirm the result is a Doc.
Given a Doc for 'três cachorros e dois gatos', retrieve the first token and create a span for 'três cachorros'.
Define tokenization and explain that spaCy's tokenizer is language-specific, giving examples.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Using lexical attributes for pattern detection
candidates.description: Token attributes like `like_num` can identify numeric tokens. Combine attributes to find patterns such as percentages.
coverage_criteria: Explain how to find tokens that represent numbers using `like_num`.
Write a loop to detect a number followed by a '%' sign.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Loading and understanding pre-trained spaCy models
candidates.description: Load pre-trained pipelines with spacy.load. Understand model packages (config, weights, strings.json) and trade-offs between blank and pre-trained models of different sizes.
coverage_criteria: Write code to load the Portuguese small pipeline and process a text, printing the Doc's text.
List what is included in a spaCy pipeline package and explain why training data is not needed.
Explain the difference between blank and pre-trained models, and compare speed/accuracy trade-offs of model sizes.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Predicting part-of-speech tags and dependencies
candidates.description: After processing text with a trained pipeline, each token has a .pos_ (coarse POS tag) and .dep_ (dependency label).
coverage_criteria: Given a Doc from a Portuguese pipeline, write a loop to print each token's text, .pos_, and .dep_.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Named entity recognition and manual correction
candidates.description: Trained pipelines identify named entities (doc.ents). When predictions miss an entity, manually create a Span for the missed tokens.
coverage_criteria: Iterate over doc.ents printing entity text and label, and use spacy.explain to describe a label.
When a model fails to recognize 'iPhone X', write code to create a Span for those two tokens.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Rule-based matching with Matcher
candidates.description: Use the Matcher class to define token-based patterns with attributes and operators for finding sequences in text.
coverage_criteria: Write code to initialize a Matcher, add a pattern that matches 'iPhone X', apply it to a Doc, and print matched spans.
Write patterns using lemmas, POS tags, and quantifiers (e.g., '+', '*', '?') to match flexible sequences.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Overview of spaCy as a production-ready NLP library
candidates.description: spaCy is an open-source MIT-licensed NLP library, maintained by Explosion.ai, supporting 73 languages and focused on production with pre-trained models.
coverage_criteria: Identify spaCy as a production-focused NLP library.
Differentiate spaCy from other libraries like NLTK (academic).
State that it supports multiple languages and offers small, medium, and large pre-trained models.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Contêineres spaCy: Doc, Token e Span
candidates.description: No spaCy, um Doc representa o documento inteiro processado, contendo uma sequência de objetos Token. Um Span é uma fatia de um Doc. Esses contêineres são a base para navegar e acessar atributos linguísticos.
coverage_criteria: Explicar o que é um Doc e como criá-lo.
Descrever Token como uma unidade individual com atributos.
Demonstrar como criar um Span usando slicing.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Atributos de tokens no spaCy: text, shape_ e is_alpha
candidates.description: Cada token possui atributos como .text, .shape_ e .is_alpha que descrevem sua forma e tipo, permitindo filtrar ou identificar padrões no texto.
coverage_criteria: Listar e definir os atributos text, shape_ e is_alpha.
Fornecer um exemplo de uso de shape_.
Usar is_alpha para separar palavras de pontuação ou números.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: POS tagging – classificação gramatical dos tokens
candidates.description: POS tagging atribui a cada token uma classe gramatical (ex.: substantivo, verbo). No spaCy, usa-se .pos_ (como NOUN, VERB) e .tag_ para detalhes mais granulares.
coverage_criteria: Explicar o que é POS tagging.
Extrair tags POS de uma frase com .pos_.
Identificar tags como PROPN, VERB em exemplos.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Lematização – redução à forma canônica
candidates.description: Lematização transforma palavras flexionadas em sua forma base (ex.: 'faz' → 'fazer'). No spaCy, acessa-se via .lemma_. Diferencia-se de stemming, que apenas corta radicais.
coverage_criteria: Definir lematização e diferenciar de stemming.
Obter o lema de um token com .lemma_.
Dar um exemplo de lematização como 'comprou' → 'comprar'.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Análise de dependências sintáticas (dep_)
candidates.description: A análise de dependências atribui a cada token um rótulo .dep_ indicando sua função sintática (ex.: nsubj para sujeito, obj para objeto). Permite visualizar a estrutura da frase com displacy.
coverage_criteria: Explicar o que .dep_ representa.
Identificar o nsubj de um verbo em uma frase.
Usar displacy.render para visualizar dependências.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Reconhecimento de Entidades Nomeadas (NER) no spaCy
candidates.description: NER identifica entidades como pessoas, organizações, locais no texto. No spaCy, acessível via doc.ents, com atributos como .label_ (PERSON, ORG, etc.).
coverage_criteria: Definir NER e listar tipos de entidades.
Extrair entidades com doc.ents.
Imprimir texto e label de cada entidade.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
